summary: The lecture covers how CPUs manage exceptions and interrupts, including mapping C++ exception handling to hardware routines. It explains out-of-order execution, the role of the reorder buffer, and how exceptions are resolved during execution. It concludes with a discussion of memory hierarchy, cache design, and locality principles that affect pipeline performance.
title: CPU Exception Handling, Out-of-Order Execution, and Memory Hierarchies

topics.title: Cache Design, Locality, and Replacement Policies

fun_fact_idea.exciting_angle: Understanding cache behavior and spatial/temporal locality lets you design AI inference services that run with minimal latency and cost—ideal for a startup building cloud‑based ML APIs that need to serve predictions in milliseconds while keeping infrastructure expenses low.
